To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extremity and homogenous of the group members are overestimated when the group is threatening.

the extremity of attitudes is overestimated and the perceived homogeneity of the group increased in the presence of a threatening group (Study 1), and that these effects are mediated by the perceived homogeneity and extremity of attitudes (Study 2).
the Group Attribution Error was stronger for a threatening group and, in particular, that participants inferred more extreme and more similar attitudes among the members.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of threat and the outcome of a vote on the perception of the extremity and homogenity of the attitudes of a group of voters.
the impact of the perceived threat on the perception and judgment of the group.
the impact of the level of threat on the extremity and homogenity of the attitudes of a group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Group Attribution Error effect is stronger for threatening groups.
threat elicits the Group Attribution Error.
the Group Attribution Error is not a general phenomenon but is moderated by the level of perceived threat of a group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Group Attribution Error is more likely to occur when the group is perceived as a threat.
the Group Attribution Error effect is more likely when the members of a minority group are perceived to be threatening.
when a group represents a threat, its members are perceived as being more similar to one another and as being more extreme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
threat is a powerful factor that can affect the way people perceive a group.
threat may influence the way people make judgments about a group.
the extremity of group members’ attitudes is overestimated in a threatening context.
